```python
import re
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st


# =========================================================
# NORMALIZATION
# =========================================================

def _normalize(value):
    return re.sub(
        r"\s+",
        " ",
        str(value).strip().lower()
    )


def _clean_columns(df):
    df = df.copy()

    df.columns = [
        str(column).strip()
        for column in df.columns
    ]

    return df


# =========================================================
# COLUMN DETECTION
# =========================================================

def _find_column(df, candidates):
    """
    Find a dataset column using exact and partial matching.
    """

    normalized = {
        _normalize(column)
        .replace(" ", "")
        .replace("_", ""): column
        for column in df.columns
    }

    # Exact match
    for candidate in candidates:

        key = (
            _normalize(candidate)
            .replace(" ", "")
            .replace("_", "")
        )

        if key in normalized:
            return normalized[key]

    # Partial match
    for column in df.columns:

        column_key = (
            _normalize(column)
            .replace(" ", "")
            .replace("_", "")
        )

        for candidate in candidates:

            candidate_key = (
                _normalize(candidate)
                .replace(" ", "")
                .replace("_", "")
            )

            if (
                candidate_key
                and candidate_key in column_key
            ):
                return column

    return None


def _numeric_columns(df):

    return (
        df
        .select_dtypes(include="number")
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )


def _categorical_columns(df):

    return (
        df
        .select_dtypes(
            include=[
                "object",
                "category",
                "string"
            ]
        )
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )


# =========================================================
# QUESTION WORD DETECTION
# =========================================================

def _comparison_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    patterns = [
        r"\bcompare\b",
        r"\bcomparison\b",
        r"\bversus\b",
        r"\bvs\b",
        r"\bdifference between\b",
        r"\bcompare between\b",
    ]

    return any(
        re.search(pattern, q)
        for pattern in patterns
    )


def _average_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "average",
            "avg",
            "mean",
        ]
    )


def _total_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "total",
            "sum",
            "overall",
        ]
    )


def _highest_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "highest",
            "maximum",
            "max",
            "top",
            "most",
            "best",
        ]
    )


def _lowest_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "lowest",
            "minimum",
            "min",
            "least",
            "worst",
            "smallest",
            "bottom",
        ]
    )


# =========================================================
# CHART INTENT DETECTION
# =========================================================

def _is_time_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "trend",
            "over time",
            "by month",
            "per month",
            "monthly",
            "month",
            "by year",
            "per year",
            "yearly",
            "year",
            "by day",
            "per day",
            "daily",
            "date",
            "dates",
            "timeline",
        ]
    )


def _is_distribution_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "distribution",
            "spread",
            "frequency",
            "histogram",
            "distribute",
        ]
    )


def _is_relationship_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "relationship",
            "correlation",
            "correlated",
            "relationship between",
            "relation between",
            "against",
        ]
    )


def _is_share_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "share",
            "percentage",
            "percent",
            "proportion",
            "contribution",
            "contribute",
            "breakdown",
        ]
    )


# =========================================================
# NUMERIC CONVERSION
# =========================================================

def _numeric(df, column):

    return pd.to_numeric(
        df[column],
        errors="coerce"
    )


# =========================================================
# FIND METRIC MENTIONED IN QUESTION
# =========================================================

def _find_metric_column(df, question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    numeric_columns = _numeric_columns(df)

    if not numeric_columns:
        return None

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Exact / partial column-name matching
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    for column in numeric_columns:

        column_text = _normalize(column)

        variants = [
            column_text,
            column_text.replace("_", " "),
            column_text.replace("_", ""),
        ]

        for variant in variants:

            if variant and variant in q:
                return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Common business metric aliases
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    aliases = {

        "sales": [
            "sales",
            "revenue",
            "turnover",
        ],

        "revenue": [
            "revenue",
            "sales",
            "turnover",
        ],

        "salary": [
            "salary",
            "salaries",
            "pay",
            "wage",
            "income",
            "compensation",
        ],

        "quantity": [
            "quantity",
            "units",
            "volume",
        ],

        "profit": [
            "profit",
            "profits",
            "margin",
        ],

        "performance": [
            "performance",
            "score",
            "rating",
        ],

        "experience": [
            "experience",
            "years",
            "tenure",
        ],

        "age": [
            "age",
        ],
    }

    for column in numeric_columns:

        column_text = _normalize(column)

        for key, words in aliases.items():

            if key in column_text:

                if any(
                    word in q
                    for word in words
                ):
                    return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # One numeric column = safest fallback
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if len(numeric_columns) == 1:
        return numeric_columns[0]

    return None


# =========================================================
# FIND DIMENSION COLUMN
# =========================================================

def _find_dimension_column(
    df,
    question,
    mentioned_values=None
):

    categorical_columns = _categorical_columns(df)

    if not categorical_columns:
        return None

    q = _normalize(question)

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Explicit column name
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    for column in categorical_columns:

        column_text = _normalize(column)

        variants = [
            column_text,
            column_text.replace("_", " "),
            column_text.replace("_", ""),
        ]

        if any(
            variant
            and variant in q
            for variant in variants
        ):
            return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Value-based detection
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if mentioned_values:

        for column in categorical_columns:

            values = (
                df[column]
                .dropna()
                .astype(str)
                .str.strip()
                .unique()
                .tolist()
            )

            normalized_values = {
                _normalize(value)
                for value in values
            }

            matches = 0

            for value in mentioned_values:

                if (
                    _normalize(value)
                    in normalized_values
                ):
                    matches += 1

            if matches >= 2:
                return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Common dimensions
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    dimension_words = [
        "department",
        "dept",
        "region",
        "area",
        "location",
        "city",
        "state",
        "country",
        "category",
        "segment",
        "product",
        "team",
        "division",
        "gender",
        "customer",
        "employee",
        "name",
    ]

    for column in categorical_columns:

        column_text = (
            _normalize(column)
            .replace("_", " ")
        )

        if any(
            word in column_text
            for word in dimension_words
        ):

            if any(
                word in q
                for word in dimension_words
            ):
                return column

    return None


# =========================================================
# FIND VALUES MENTIONED IN QUESTION
# =========================================================

def _mentioned_values(
    df,
    column,
    question
):

    question_text = _normalize(question)

    values = (
        df[column]
        .dropna()
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
        .unique()
        .tolist()
    )

    matches = []

    for value in values:

        value_text = _normalize(value)

        if not value_text:
            continue

        pattern = (
            r"(?<!\w)"
            + re.escape(value_text)
            + r"(?!\w)"
        )

        match = re.search(
            pattern,
            question_text
        )

        if match:

            matches.append(
                (
                    match.start(),
                    value
                )
            )

    matches.sort(
        key=lambda item: item[0]
    )

    result = []
    seen = set()

    for _, value in matches:

        key = _normalize(value)

        if key not in seen:

            seen.add(key)
            result.append(value)

    return result


# =========================================================
# FIND TOP N
# =========================================================

def _get_requested_limit(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    # top 5
    match = re.search(
        r"\btop\s+(\d+)\b",
        q
    )

    if match:
        return int(match.group(1))

    # bottom 5
    match = re.search(
        r"\bbottom\s+(\d+)\b",
        q
    )

    if match:
        return int(match.group(1))

    # first 5
    match = re.search(
        r"\b(?:first|highest|lowest)\s+(\d+)\b",
        q
    )

    if match:
        return int(match.group(1))

    return 1


# =========================================================
# CHART RENDERER
# =========================================================

def _render_chart(
    data,
    chart_type,
    title=None,
    dimension_col=None,
    metric_col=None
):

    if data is None or data.empty:
        return False

    if title:

        st.markdown(
            f"### 📊 {title}"
        )

    # =====================================================
    # BAR
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "bar":

        st.bar_chart(
            data,
            use_container_width=True
        )

        return True

    # =====================================================
    # LINE
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "line":

        st.line_chart(
            data,
            use_container_width=True
        )

        return True

    # =====================================================
    # SCATTER
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "scatter":

        try:

            import plotly.express as px

            if (
                dimension_col is None
                or metric_col is None
            ):
                return False

            plot_data = data.copy()

            fig = px.scatter(
                plot_data,
                x=dimension_col,
                y=metric_col,
                title=None,
            )

            fig.update_layout(
                margin=dict(
                    l=20,
                    r=20,
                    t=20,
                    b=20
                )
            )

            st.plotly_chart(
                fig,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        except Exception:

            st.scatter_chart(
                data,
                x=dimension_col,
                y=metric_col,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

    # =====================================================
    # PIE
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "pie":

        try:

            import plotly.express as px

            if (
                dimension_col is None
                or metric_col is None
            ):
                return False

            plot_data = data.copy()

            fig = px.pie(
                plot_data,
                names=dimension_col,
                values=metric_col,
            )

            fig.update_layout(
                margin=dict(
                    l=20,
                    r=20,
                    t=20,
                    b=20
                )
            )

            st.plotly_chart(
                fig,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        except Exception:

            st.bar_chart(
                data.set_index(
                    dimension_col
                )[metric_col],
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

    # =====================================================
    # HISTOGRAM
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "histogram":

        try:

            import plotly.express as px

            plot_data = data.copy()

            fig = px.histogram(
                plot_data,
                x=metric_col,
                nbins=20,
            )

            fig.update_layout(
                margin=dict(
                    l=20,
                    r=20,
                    t=20,
                    b=20
                )
            )

            st.plotly_chart(
                fig,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        except Exception:

            histogram = (
                data[metric_col]
                .dropna()
                .value_counts()
                .sort_index()
            )

            st.bar_chart(
                histogram,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

    return False


# =========================================================
# INTELLIGENT CHART SELECTION
# =========================================================

def _choose_chart_type(
    question,
    dimension_col=None,
    metric_col=None,
    df=None
):

    if _is_distribution_question(question):

        return "histogram"

    if _is_relationship_question(question):

        if (
            df is not None
            and len(_numeric_columns(df)) >= 2
        ):
            return "scatter"

    if _is_time_question(question):

        return "line"

    if _is_share_question(question):

        return "pie"

    if _comparison_requested(question):

        return "bar"

    if (
        _highest_requested(question)
        or _lowest_requested(question)
    ):

        return "bar"

    if (
        dimension_col is not None
        and metric_col is not None
    ):

        return "bar"

    return "bar"


# =========================================================
# GENERIC GROUPED VISUALIZATION
# =========================================================

def _show_grouped(
    df,
    dimension_col,
    metric_col,
    aggregation,
    title,
    question=None
):

    data = df.copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            dimension_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    if data.empty:
        return False

    if aggregation == "mean":

        grouped = (
            data
            .groupby(dimension_col)[metric_col]
            .mean()
        )

        label = "Average"

    elif aggregation == "count":

        grouped = (
            data
            .groupby(dimension_col)[metric_col]
            .count()
        )

        label = "Count"

    else:

        grouped = (
            data
            .groupby(dimension_col)[metric_col]
            .sum()
        )

        label = "Total"

    grouped = (
        grouped
        .sort_values(
            ascending=False
        )
        .head(20)
    )

    if grouped.empty:
        return False

    chart_type = _choose_chart_type(
        question or "",
        dimension_col,
        metric_col,
        df
    )

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # PIE
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if chart_type == "pie":

        chart_data = (
            grouped
            .reset_index()
        )

        _render_chart(
            chart_data,
            "pie",
            title,
            dimension_col,
            metric_col
        )

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # LINE
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    elif chart_type == "line":

        chart_data = (
            grouped
            .rename(
                f"{label} {metric_col}"
            )
            .to_frame()
        )

        _render_chart(
            chart_data,
            "line",
            title,
            dimension_col,
            metric_col
        )

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # BAR
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    else:

        chart_data = (
            grouped
            .rename(
                f"{label} {metric_col}"
            )
        )

        _render_chart(
            chart_data,
            "bar",
            title,
            dimension_col,
            metric_col
        )

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # TABLE
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    table = (
        grouped
        .rename("Value")
        .reset_index()
    )

    st.dataframe(
        table,
        use_container_width=True,
        hide_index=True
    )

    return True


# =========================================================
# GENERIC COMPARISON
# =========================================================

def _show_generic_comparison(
    df,
    question,
    dimension_col,
    metric_col
):

    values = _mentioned_values(
        df,
        dimension_col,
        question
    )

    if len(values) < 2:
        return False

    selected = values[:2]

    data = df.copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data["__dimension__"] = (
        data[dimension_col]
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
    )

        subset=[
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    data = data[
        data["__dimension__"].isin(

    if data.empty:

    q = _normalize(question)

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Aggregation
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if (

# =========================================================

def _show_threshold(
    df,
    question,
    person_col,
    metric_col
):

    q = _normalize(question)

    patterns = [

        (
            r"(?:more than|greater than|above|over|exceeding)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            ">"
        ),

        (
            r"(?:less than|below|under)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            "<"
        ),

        (
            r"(?:at least|minimum of)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            ">="
        ),

        (
            r"(?:at most|maximum of)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            "<="
        ),
    ]

    operator = None
    threshold = None

    for pattern, op in patterns:

        match = re.search(
            pattern,
            q
        )

        if match:

            threshold = float(
                match.group(1)
                .replace(",", "")
            )

            operator = op

            break

    if operator is None:
        return False

    data = df[
        [
            person_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    ].copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            person_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    if operator == ">":

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] > threshold
        ]

    elif operator == "<":

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] < threshold
        ]

    elif operator == ">=":

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] >= threshold
        ]

    else:

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] <= threshold
        ]

    result = result.sort_values(
        metric_col,
        ascending=False
    )

    st.markdown(
        f"### 📊 {metric_col} "
        f"{operator} "
        f"{threshold:,.0f}"
    )

    if result.empty:

        st.info(
            "No matching records were found."
        )

    else:

        st.dataframe(
            result,
            use_container_width=True,
            hide_index=True
        )

        chart_data = (
            result
            .set_index(person_col)[
                metric_col
            ]
        )

        _render_chart(
            chart_data,
            "bar"
        )

    return True

def _find_date_column(df, question):

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Actual datetime columns
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    datetime_columns = (
        df
        .select_dtypes(
            include=[
                "datetime",
                "datetimetz"
            ]
        )
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )

    if datetime_columns:
        return datetime_columns[0]

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Date-like column names
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    candidates = [
        "date",
        "datetime",
        "timestamp",
        "month",
        "year",
        "time",
    ]

    for column in df.columns:

        column_text = _normalize(
            column
        )

        if any(
            candidate in column_text
            for candidate in candidates
        ):

            converted = pd.to_datetime(
                df[column],
                errors="coerce"
            )

            if converted.notna().sum() >= 2:

                return column

    return None

def _find_second_numeric_column(
    df,
    question,
    first_metric
):

    numeric_columns = _numeric_columns(
        df
    )

    remaining = [
        column
        for column in numeric_columns
        if column != first_metric
    ]

    if not remaining:
        return None

    q = _normalize(question)

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Explicitly mentioned column
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    for column in remaining:

        column_text = _normalize(
            column
        )

        if column_text in q:
            return column

        if (
            column_text.replace("_", " ")
            in q
        ):

            return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Common pairs
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    pairs = [

        (
            "salary",
            [
                "experience",
                "age",
                "performance"
            ]
        ),

        (
            "sales",
            [
                "profit",
                "quantity",
                "units"
            ]
        ),

        (
            "experience",
            [
                "salary",
                "performance",
                "age"
            ]
        ),
    ]

    first_text = _normalize(
        first_metric
    )

    for key, possible_columns in pairs:

        if key in first_text:

            for column in remaining:

                column_text = _normalize(
                    column
                )

                if any(
                    item in column_text
                    for item in possible_columns
                ):

                    return column

    return remaining[0]

# =========================================================
# MAIN VISUALIZATION ENGINE
# =========================================================

def generate_visual_analysis(
    df,
    question=None
):
    """
    Generic AI-style visualization engine.

    Supported chart types:

    - Bar
    - Line
    - Pie
    - Scatter
    - Histogram

    Supported analysis:

    - Category comparison
    - Metric comparison
    - Average
    - Total
    - Highest
    - Lowest
    - Top N
    - Bottom N
    - Threshold
    - Distribution
    - Trend
    - Share
    - Correlation
    - Grouped analysis
    """

    # =====================================================
    # VALIDATION
    # =====================================================

    if (
        df is None
        or df.empty
        or not question
    ):

        return False

    data = _clean_columns(
        df
    )

    question = str(
        question
    ).strip()

    q = _normalize(
        question
    )

    numeric_columns = _numeric_columns(
        data
    )

    categorical_columns = _categorical_columns(
        data
    )

    if not numeric_columns:
        return False

    # =====================================================
    # FIND METRIC
    # =====================================================

    metric_col = _find_metric_column(
        data,
        question
    )

    if metric_col is None:

        metric_col = numeric_columns[0]

    # =====================================================
    # FIND DIMENSION
    # =====================================================

    dimension_col = None

    if categorical_columns:

        # -------------------------------------------------
        # First check explicitly mentioned values
        # -------------------------------------------------

        for column in categorical_columns:

            values = _mentioned_values(
                data,
                column,
                question
            )

            if len(values) >= 2:

                dimension_col = column

                break

        # -------------------------------------------------
        # Otherwise normal dimension detection
        # -------------------------------------------------

        if dimension_col is None:

            dimension_col = _find_dimension_column(
                data,
                question
            )

    # =====================================================
    # 1. DISTRIBUTION
    # =====================================================

    if _is_distribution_question(
        question
    ):

        if _show_histogram(
            data,
            question,
            metric_col
        ):

            return True

    # =====================================================
```

Yes — this output shows the **multi-question input is not being handled correctly yet**.

The problem is that your app sends the entire paragraph as **one question**:

> `Who is the highest paid employee? Who has the highest performance score? ...`

Your `analysis_engine.py` then tries to interpret all of it as a single intent, so the verified result becomes unreliable.

### What we should change

Make the system automatically split multiple questions and analyze each independently:

```text
User:
Who is the highest paid employee?
Who has the highest performance score?
Who has the most experience?
What is Asha's salary?
Which employees earn more than 70000?
Which department has the highest average salary?
```

Then Python should produce **six separate verified calculations**:

```text
Question 1
→ Highest paid employee
→ Arun
→ Salary: 85,000

Question 2
→ Highest performance score
→ [actual employee]
→ [actual score]

Question 3
→ Most experience
→ [actual employee]
→ [actual years]

Question 4
→ Asha's salary
→ [actual salary]

Question 5
→ Employees earning > 70,000
→ [actual employees]

Question 6
→ Highest average salary department
→ Finance
→ Average: 80,000
```

Then Ollama receives those **six verified results** and only converts them into a readable answer.

### Important

We should **not** let Ollama figure out the answers from the combined question. Your Python analysis engine must calculate every answer first. Otherwise you'll keep getting errors like:

> "Asha's salary is unknown"

or

> "There is no department with the highest average salary"

when the dataset actually contains the required information.

**So the next change should be the multi-question processing layer in `app.py` + the corresponding employee/threshold handling in `analysis_engine.py`.**

```python
import re
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st


# =========================================================
# NORMALIZATION
# =========================================================

def _normalize(value):
    return re.sub(
        r"\s+",
        " ",
        str(value).strip().lower()
    )


def _clean_columns(df):
    df = df.copy()

    df.columns = [
        str(column).strip()
        for column in df.columns
    ]

    return df


# =========================================================
# COLUMN DETECTION
# =========================================================

def _find_column(df, candidates):
    """
    Find a dataset column using exact and partial matching.
    """

    normalized = {
        _normalize(column)
        .replace(" ", "")
        .replace("_", ""): column
        for column in df.columns
    }

    # Exact match
    for candidate in candidates:

        key = (
            _normalize(candidate)
            .replace(" ", "")
            .replace("_", "")
        )

        if key in normalized:
            return normalized[key]

    # Partial match
    for column in df.columns:

        column_key = (
            _normalize(column)
            .replace(" ", "")
            .replace("_", "")
        )

        for candidate in candidates:

            candidate_key = (
                _normalize(candidate)
                .replace(" ", "")
                .replace("_", "")
            )

            if (
                candidate_key
                and candidate_key in column_key
            ):
                return column

    return None


def _numeric_columns(df):
    return (
        df
        .select_dtypes(include="number")
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )


def _categorical_columns(df):
    return (
        df
        .select_dtypes(
            include=[
                "object",
                "category",
                "string"
            ]
        )
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )


# =========================================================
# QUESTION WORD DETECTION
# =========================================================

def _comparison_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    patterns = [
        r"\bcompare\b",
        r"\bcomparison\b",
        r"\bversus\b",
        r"\bvs\b",
        r"\bdifference between\b",
        r"\bcompare between\b",
    ]

    return any(
        re.search(pattern, q)
        for pattern in patterns
    )


def _average_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "average",
            "avg",
            "mean",
        ]
    )


def _total_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "total",
            "sum",
            "overall",
        ]
    )


def _highest_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "highest",
            "maximum",
            "max",
            "top",
            "most",
            "best",
        ]
    )


def _lowest_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "lowest",
            "minimum",
            "min",
            "least",
            "worst",
            "smallest",
        ]
    )


# =========================================================
# CHART INTENT DETECTION
# =========================================================

def _is_time_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "trend",
            "over time",
            "by month",
            "per month",
            "monthly",
            "month",
            "by year",
            "per year",
            "yearly",
            "year",
            "by day",
            "per day",
            "daily",
            "date",
            "dates",
            "timeline",
        ]
    )


def _is_distribution_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "distribution",
            "spread",
            "frequency",
            "histogram",
            "distribute",
        ]
    )


def _is_relationship_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "relationship",
            "correlation",
            "correlated",
            "relationship between",
            "relation between",
            "against",
        ]
    )


def _is_share_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "share",
            "percentage",
            "percent",
            "proportion",
            "contribution",
            "contribute",
            "breakdown",
        ]
    )


# =========================================================
# NUMERIC CONVERSION
# =========================================================

def _numeric(df, column):

    return pd.to_numeric(
        df[column],
        errors="coerce"
    )


# =========================================================
# FIND METRIC MENTIONED IN QUESTION
# =========================================================

def _find_metric_column(df, question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    numeric_columns = _numeric_columns(df)

    if not numeric_columns:
        return None

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Exact / partial column-name matching
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    for column in numeric_columns:

        column_text = _normalize(column)

        variants = [
            column_text,
            column_text.replace("_", " "),
            column_text.replace("_", ""),
        ]

        for variant in variants:

            if variant and variant in q:
                return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Common business metric aliases
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    aliases = {

        "sales": [
            "sales",
            "revenue",
            "turnover",
        ],

        "revenue": [
            "revenue",
            "sales",
            "turnover",
        ],

        "salary": [
            "salary",
            "salaries",
            "pay",
            "wage",
            "income",
            "compensation",
        ],

        "quantity": [
            "quantity",
            "units",
            "volume",
        ],

        "profit": [
            "profit",
            "profits",
            "margin",
        ],

        "performance": [
            "performance",
            "score",
            "rating",
        ],

        "experience": [
            "experience",
            "years",
            "tenure",
        ],

        "age": [
            "age",
        ],
    }

    for column in numeric_columns:

        column_text = _normalize(column)

        for key, words in aliases.items():

            if key in column_text:

                if any(
                    word in q
                    for word in words
                ):
                    return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # One numeric column = safest fallback
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if len(numeric_columns) == 1:
        return numeric_columns[0]

    return None


# =========================================================
# FIND DIMENSION COLUMN
# =========================================================

def _find_dimension_column(
    df,
    question,
    mentioned_values=None
):

    categorical_columns = _categorical_columns(df)

    if not categorical_columns:
        return None

    q = _normalize(question)

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Explicit column name
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    for column in categorical_columns:

        column_text = _normalize(column)

        variants = [
            column_text,
            column_text.replace("_", " "),
            column_text.replace("_", ""),
        ]

        if any(
            variant
            and variant in q
            for variant in variants
        ):
            return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Value-based detection
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if mentioned_values:

        for column in categorical_columns:

            values = (
                df[column]
                .dropna()
                .astype(str)
                .str.strip()
                .unique()
                .tolist()
            )

            normalized_values = {
                _normalize(value)
                for value in values
            }

            matches = 0

            for value in mentioned_values:

                if (
                    _normalize(value)
                    in normalized_values
                ):
                    matches += 1

            if matches >= 2:
                return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Common dimensions
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    dimension_words = [
        "department",
        "dept",
        "region",
        "area",
        "location",
        "city",
        "state",
        "country",
        "category",
        "segment",
        "product",
        "team",
        "division",
        "gender",
        "customer",
        "employee",
        "name",
    ]

    for column in categorical_columns:

        column_text = (
            _normalize(column)
            .replace("_", " ")
        )

        if any(
            word in column_text
            for word in dimension_words
        ):

            if any(
                word in q
                for word in dimension_words
            ):
                return column

    return None


# =========================================================
# FIND VALUES MENTIONED IN QUESTION
# =========================================================

def _mentioned_values(
    df,
    column,
    question
):

    question_text = _normalize(question)

    values = (
        df[column]
        .dropna()
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
        .unique()
        .tolist()
    )

    matches = []

    for value in values:

        value_text = _normalize(value)

        if not value_text:
            continue

        pattern = (
            r"(?<!\w)"
            + re.escape(value_text)
            + r"(?!\w)"
        )

        match = re.search(
            pattern,
            question_text
        )

        if match:

            matches.append(
                (
                    match.start(),
                    value
                )
            )

    matches.sort(
        key=lambda item: item[0]
    )

    result = []
    seen = set()

    for _, value in matches:

        key = _normalize(value)

        if key not in seen:

            seen.add(key)
            result.append(value)

    return result


# =========================================================
# CHART RENDERER
# =========================================================

def _render_chart(
    data,
    chart_type,
    title=None,
    dimension_col=None,
    metric_col=None
):
    """
    Central chart rendering function.

    Supported:
        bar
        line
        pie
        scatter
        histogram
    """

    if data is None or data.empty:
        return False

    if title:
        st.markdown(
            f"### 📊 {title}"
        )

    # =====================================================
    # BAR
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "bar":

        st.bar_chart(
            data,
            use_container_width=True
        )

        return True

    # =====================================================
    # LINE
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "line":

        st.line_chart(
            data,
            use_container_width=True
        )

        return True

    # =====================================================
    # SCATTER
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "scatter":

        try:

            import plotly.express as px

            if (
                dimension_col is None
                or metric_col is None
            ):
                return False

            plot_data = data.copy()

            fig = px.scatter(
                plot_data,
                x=dimension_col,
                y=metric_col,
                title=None,
            )

            fig.update_layout(
                margin=dict(
                    l=20,
                    r=20,
                    t=20,
                    b=20
                )
            )

            st.plotly_chart(
                fig,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        except Exception:

            # Graceful fallback
            st.scatter_chart(
                data,
                x=dimension_col,
                y=metric_col,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

    # =====================================================
    # PIE
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "pie":

        try:

            import plotly.express as px

            if (
                dimension_col is None
                or metric_col is None
            ):
                return False

            plot_data = data.copy()

            fig = px.pie(
                plot_data,
                names=dimension_col,
                values=metric_col,
            )

            fig.update_layout(
                margin=dict(
                    l=20,
                    r=20,
                    t=20,
                    b=20
                )
            )

            st.plotly_chart(
                fig,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        except Exception:

            # If Plotly isn't installed,
            # use a bar chart instead.
            st.bar_chart(
                data.set_index(
                    dimension_col
                )[metric_col],
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

    # =====================================================
    # HISTOGRAM
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "histogram":

        try:

            import plotly.express as px

            plot_data = data.copy()

            fig = px.histogram(
                plot_data,
                x=metric_col,
                nbins=20,
            )

            fig.update_layout(
                margin=dict(
                    l=20,
                    r=20,
                    t=20,
                    b=20
                )
            )

            st.plotly_chart(
                fig,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        except Exception:

            # Fallback histogram using
            # pandas value counts.

            histogram = (
                data[metric_col]
                .dropna()
                .value_counts()
                .sort_index()
            )

            st.bar_chart(
                histogram,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

    return False


# =========================================================
# INTELLIGENT CHART SELECTION
# =========================================================

def _choose_chart_type(
    question,
    dimension_col=None,
    metric_col=None,
    df=None
):
    """
    Decide the most appropriate chart based
    on the question and dataset structure.
    """

    q = _normalize(question)

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Distribution
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if _is_distribution_question(question):

        return "histogram"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Relationship / correlation
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if _is_relationship_question(question):

            and len(_numeric_columns(df)) >= 2
        ):
            return "scatter"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Time / trend
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if _is_time_question(question):

        return "line"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Share / percentage
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if _is_share_question(question):

        return "pie"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Comparison
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if _comparison_requested(question):

        return "bar"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Highest / lowest / top
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if (
        _highest_requested(question)
        or _lowest_requested(question)
    ):

        return "bar"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Grouped categorical analysis
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if (
        dimension_col is not None
        and metric_col is not None
    ):

        return "bar"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Default
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    return "bar"

# =========================================================

def _show_threshold(
    df,
    question,
    person_col,
    metric_col
):

    q = _normalize(question)

    patterns = [

        (
            r"(?:more than|greater than|above|over|exceeding)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            ">"
        ),

        (
            r"(?:less than|below|under)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            "<"
        ),

        (
            r"(?:at least|minimum of)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            ">="
        ),

        (
            r"(?:at most|maximum of)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            "<="
        ),
    ]

    operator = None
    threshold = None

    for pattern, op in patterns:

        match = re.search(
            pattern,
            q
        )

        if match:

            threshold = float(
                match.group(1)
                .replace(",", "")
            )

            operator = op

            break

    if operator is None:
        return False

    data = df[
        [
            person_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    ].copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            person_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    if operator == ">":

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] > threshold
        ]

    elif operator == "<":

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] < threshold
        ]

    elif operator == ">=":

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] >= threshold
        ]

    else:

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] <= threshold
        ]

    result = result.sort_values(
        metric_col,
        ascending=False
    )

    st.markdown(
        f"### 📊 {metric_col} "
        f"{operator} "
        f"{threshold:,.0f}"
    )

    if result.empty:

        st.info(
            "No matching records were found."
        )

    else:

        st.dataframe(
            result,
            use_container_width=True,
            hide_index=True
        )

        chart_data = (
            result
            .set_index(person_col)[
                metric_col
            ]
        )

        _render_chart(
            chart_data,
            "bar"
        )

    return True

def _find_date_column(df, question):

    # First look for actual datetime columns
    datetime_columns = (
        df
        .select_dtypes(
            include=[
                "datetime",
                "datetimetz"
            ]
        )
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )

    if datetime_columns:
        return datetime_columns[0]

    # Look for date-like column names
    candidates = [
        "date",
        "datetime",
        "timestamp",
        "month",
        "year",
        "time",
    ]

    for column in df.columns:

        column_text = _normalize(
            column
        )

        if any(
            candidate in column_text
            for candidate in candidates
        ):

            converted = pd.to_datetime(
                df[column],
                errors="coerce"
            )

            if converted.notna().sum() >= 2:
                return column

    return None

def _find_second_numeric_column(
    df,
    question,
    first_metric
):

    numeric_columns = _numeric_columns(
        df
    )

    remaining = [
        column
        for column in numeric_columns
        if column != first_metric
    ]

    if not remaining:
        return None

    q = _normalize(question)

    # Prefer a column explicitly mentioned
    for column in remaining:

        column_text = _normalize(
            column
        )

        if column_text in q:

            return column

        if (
            column_text.replace("_", " ")
            in q
        ):

            return column

    # Common pairs
    pairs = [
        (
            "salary",
            [
                "experience",
                "age",
                "performance"
            ]
        ),

        (
            "sales",
            [
                "profit",
                "quantity",
                "units"
            ]
        ),

        (
            "experience",
            [
                "salary",
                "performance",
                "age"
            ]
        ),
    ]

    first_text = _normalize(
        first_metric
    )

    for key, possible_columns in pairs:

        if key in first_text:

            for column in remaining:

                column_text = _normalize(
                    column
                )

                if any(
                    item in column_text
                    for item in possible_columns
                ):

                    return column

    return remaining[0]


def _show_scatter(

):

    second_metric = _find_second_numeric_column(

    try:

# =========================================================
# MAIN VISUALIZATION ENGINE
# =========================================================

def generate_visual_analysis(
    df,
    question=None
):
    """
    Generic AI-style visualization engine.

    Supported chart types:

    - Bar
    - Line
    - Pie
    - Scatter
    - Histogram

    Supported analysis:

    - Category comparison
    - Metric comparison
    - Average
    - Total
    - Highest
    - Lowest
    - Top N
    - Threshold
    - Distribution
    - Trend
    - Share
    - Correlation
    - Grouped analysis

    Returns:

        True
            Visualization created.

        False
            No suitable visualization found.
    """

    # =====================================================
    # VALIDATION
    # =====================================================

    if (
        df is None
        or df.empty
        or not question
    ):

        return False

    data = _clean_columns(
        df
    )

    question = str(
        question
    ).strip()

    q = _normalize(
        question
    )

    numeric_columns = _numeric_columns(
        data
    )

    categorical_columns = _categorical_columns(
        data
    )

    if not numeric_columns:
        return False

    # =====================================================
    # FIND METRIC
    # =====================================================

    metric_col = _find_metric_column(
        data,
        question
    )

    if metric_col is None:
        metric_col = numeric_columns[0]

    # =====================================================
    # FIND DIMENSION
    # =====================================================

    dimension_col = None

    if categorical_columns:

        # First try values explicitly mentioned
        # in the question.

        for column in categorical_columns:

            values = _mentioned_values(
                data,
                column,
                question
            )

            if len(values) >= 2:

                dimension_col = column

                break

        # Otherwise use normal dimension detection.

        if dimension_col is None:

            dimension_col = _find_dimension_column(
                data,
                question
            )

    # =====================================================
    # 1. DISTRIBUTION
    # =====================================================

    if _is_distribution_question(
        question
    ):

        if _show_histogram(
            data,
            question,
            metric_col
        ):

            return True

    # =====================================================
    # 2. RELATIONSHIP / CORRELATION
    # =====================================================

    if _is_relationship_question(
        question
    ):

        if _show_scatter(
            data,
            question,
            metric_col
        ):

            return True

    # =====================================================
    # 3. TIME / TREND
    # =====================================================

    if _is_time_question(
        question
    ):

        if _show_time_series(
            data,
            question,
            metric_col
        ):

            return True

    # =====================================================
    # 4. SHARE / PERCENTAGE
    # =====================================================

    if (
        _is_share_question(
            question
        )
        and dimension_col
        and metric_col
```

```python
# =========================================================
# SMART CHART SELECTION
# =========================================================

def _choose_chart_type(
    question,
    dimension_col=None,
    metric_col=None,
    second_metric_col=None
):
    """
    Automatically choose the most suitable visualization
    based on the question and available data.
    """

    q = _normalize(question)

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Numeric relationship
    # Example:
    # "What is the relationship between sales and profit?"
    # "Sales against profit"
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if second_metric_col is not None:

        if any(
            phrase in q
            for phrase in (
                "relationship",
                "correlation",
                "against",
                "relationship between",
            )
        ):
            return "scatter"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Time-series / trend
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    trend_words = (
        "trend",
        "over time",
        "time series",
        "monthly trend",
        "daily trend",
        "weekly trend",
        "yearly trend",
        "growth over time",
        "sales over time",
        "revenue over time",
    )

    if any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in trend_words
    ):
        return "line"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Percentage / share / distribution
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    share_words = (
        "percentage",
        "percent",
        "share",
        "proportion",
        "percentage of",
        "share of",
    )

    if any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in share_words
    ):
        return "pie"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Category comparison
    #
    # IMPORTANT:
    # "North vs South sales"
    # stays BAR.
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if _comparison_requested(question):
        return "bar"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Ranking
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if (
        _highest_requested(question)
        or _lowest_requested(question)
    ):
        return "bar"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Default
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    return "bar"
```

# 2. Add the chart renderer

Put this **directly below `_choose_chart_type()`**:

```python
# =========================================================
# SMART CHART RENDERER
# =========================================================

def _render_chart(
    data,
    chart_type,
    dimension_col,
    metric_col,
    title=None
):
    """
    Render the selected visualization type.
    """

    if data is None or data.empty:
        return False

    chart_data = data.copy()

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # BAR
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if chart_type == "bar":

        if dimension_col in chart_data.columns:

            chart_data = (
                chart_data
                .set_index(dimension_col)
            )

        st.bar_chart(
            chart_data[metric_col],
            use_container_width=True
        )

        return True

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # LINE
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if chart_type == "line":

        if dimension_col in chart_data.columns:

            chart_data = (
                chart_data
                .set_index(dimension_col)
            )

        st.line_chart(
            chart_data[metric_col],
            use_container_width=True
        )

        return True

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # SCATTER
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if chart_type == "scatter":

        numeric = chart_data[
            [dimension_col, metric_col]
        ].copy()

        numeric[dimension_col] = pd.to_numeric(
            numeric[dimension_col],
            errors="coerce"
        )

        numeric[metric_col] = pd.to_numeric(
            numeric[metric_col],
            errors="coerce"
        )

        numeric = numeric.dropna()

        if numeric.empty:
            return False

        st.scatter_chart(
            numeric,
            x=dimension_col,
            y=metric_col,
            use_container_width=True
        )

        return True

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # PIE
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if chart_type == "pie":

        pie_data = (
            chart_data[
                [dimension_col, metric_col]
            ]
            .copy()
        )

        pie_data[metric_col] = pd.to_numeric(
            pie_data[metric_col],
            errors="coerce"
        )

        pie_data = pie_data.dropna(
            subset=[metric_col]
        )

        if pie_data.empty:
            return False

        # Vega-Lite pie chart.
        spec = {
            "mark": {
                "type": "arc",
                "tooltip": True
            },
            "encoding": {
                "theta": {
                    "field": metric_col,
                    "type": "quantitative"
                },
                "color": {
                    "field": dimension_col,
                    "type": "nominal"
                },
                "tooltip": [
                    {
                        "field": dimension_col,
                        "type": "nominal"
                    },
                    {
                        "field": metric_col,
                        "type": "quantitative"
                    }
                ]
            }
        }

        st.vega_lite_chart(
            pie_data,
            spec=spec,
            use_container_width=True
        )

        return True

    return False
```

```python
import re

def normalize(value):
    """Normalize text for matching."""

    return re.sub(
        r"\s+",
        " ",
        str(value).strip().lower()
    )


def clean_column_name(value):
    """Normalize column names for matching."""

    return (
        normalize(value)
        .replace("_", "")
        .replace("-", "")
        .replace(" ", "")
    )


def clean_dataframe(df):
    """Return a safe dataframe copy."""

    data = df.copy()

    data.columns = [
        str(column).strip()

    ]

def numeric_columns(df):
    """Return numeric columns."""

        df

def categorical_columns(df):

            ]

def safe_float(value):

def format_value(value):

    number = safe_float(value)

    if number is None:

    if abs(number) >= 1_000_000:

        key = clean_column_name(name)

        matches = mentioned_values(
            df,
            column,
            question
        )

        if len(matches) > best_matches:

            best_matches = len(matches)
            best_column = column

    if best_column is not None:
        return best_column

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Dimension aliases
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    for column in cats:

        column_key = clean_column_name(column)

        for alias in DIMENSION_ALIASES:

            alias_key = clean_column_name(alias)

            if alias_key in column_key:

                if (
                    alias in q
                    or alias.rstrip("s") in q
                ):
                    return column

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Business-friendly categorical column
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    candidates = []

    for column in cats:

        unique_count = (
            df[column]
            .dropna()
            .nunique()
        )

        if 2 <= unique_count <= 50:

            candidates.append(
                (
                    unique_count,
                    column
                )
            )

    if candidates:

        # Prefer the lowest-cardinality sensible dimension
        candidates.sort(
            key=lambda x: x[0]
        )

        return candidates[0][1]

    return None

def extract_top_n(question):

    q = normalize(question)

    patterns = [
        r"\btop\s+(\d+)",
        r"\bbottom\s+(\d+)",
        r"\bfirst\s+(\d+)",
        r"\blast\s+(\d+)"
    ]

    for pattern in patterns:

        match = re.search(
            pattern,
            q
        )

        if match:

            return max(
                1,
                int(match.group(1))
            )

    return 1

def find_date_column(df):

    # Real datetime columns
    datetime_columns = (
        df
        .select_dtypes(
            include=[
                "datetime",
                "datetimetz"
            ]
        )
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )

    if datetime_columns:
        return datetime_columns[0]

    # Date-like column names
    date_words = [
        "date",
        "datetime",
        "timestamp",
        "month",
        "year",
        "time"
    ]

    for column in df.columns:

        column_text = normalize(column)

        if any(
            word in column_text
            for word in date_words
        ):

            converted = pd.to_datetime(
                df[column],
                errors="coerce"
            )

            if (
                converted.notna().mean()
                >= 0.50
            ):
                return column

    # Object columns
    for column in categorical_columns(df):

        converted = pd.to_datetime(
            df[column],
            errors="coerce"
        )

        if (
            converted.notna().mean()
            >= 0.70
        ):
            return column

    return None

# 5. AGGREGATION
# ============================================================

def determine_aggregation(question):

    if average_requested(question):
        return "mean"

    if total_requested(question):
        return "sum"

    return "sum"


def aggregate_grouped(
    df,
    dimension,
    metric,
    aggregation="sum"
):

    if (
        dimension is None
        or metric is None
        or dimension not in df.columns
        or metric not in df.columns
    ):
        return pd.Series(dtype="float64")

    data = df.copy()

    data[metric] = numeric_series(
        data,
        metric
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            dimension,
            metric
        ]
    )

    if data.empty:
        return pd.Series(dtype="float64")

    grouped_object = (
        data
        .groupby(
            dimension,
            dropna=True
        )[metric]
    )

    if aggregation == "mean":

        result = grouped_object.mean()

    elif aggregation == "count":

        result = grouped_object.count()

    elif aggregation == "min":

        result = grouped_object.min()

    elif aggregation == "max":

        result = grouped_object.max()

    else:

        result = grouped_object.sum()

    return result.dropna()


# ============================================================
# SECOND NUMERIC COLUMN
# ============================================================

def find_second_numeric_column(
    df,
    question,
    first_metric
):

    nums = numeric_columns(df)

    remaining = [
        column
        for column in nums
        if column != first_metric
    ]

    if not remaining:
        return None

    q = normalize(question)

    # Explicit mention
    for column in remaining:

        column_text = normalize(column)

        if column_text in q:
            return column

        if (
            column_text.replace("_", " ")
            in q
        ):
            return column

    # Relationship hints
    relationship_pairs = {

        "sales": [
            "profit",
            "quantity",
            "units",
            "price"
        ],

        "revenue": [
            "profit",
            "quantity",
            "price"
        ],

        "salary": [
            "experience",
            "age",
            "performance"
        ],

        "experience": [
            "salary",
            "performance",
            "age"
        ],

        "price": [
            "quantity",
            "sales",
            "revenue"
        ]
    }

    first_text = normalize(
        first_metric
    )

    for key, possible in relationship_pairs.items():

        if key in first_text:

            for column in remaining:

                column_text = normalize(
                    column
                )

                if any(
                    item in column_text
                    for item in possible
                ):
                    return column

    return remaining[0]

def _plotly_available():

    try:

        return True

def render_chart(
    data,
    chart_type,
    title=None,
    x=None,
    y=None
):

    if data is None:
        return False

    if isinstance(data, pd.Series):

        if data.empty:
            return False

        chart_df = (
            data
            .rename("Value")
            .reset_index()
        )

        chart_df.columns = [
            "Category",
            "Value"
        ]

        x = "Category"
        y = "Value"

    else:

        if data.empty:
            return False

        chart_df = data.copy()

    if title:
        st.markdown(
            f"### 📊 {title}"
        )

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # PLOTLY
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if _plotly_available():

        try:

            import plotly.express as px

            if chart_type == "bar":

                fig = px.bar(
                    chart_df,
                    x=x,
                    y=y,
                    text=y
                )

                fig.update_traces(
                    texttemplate="%{text:,.0f}",
                    textposition="outside",
                    cliponaxis=False
                )

            elif chart_type == "line":

                fig = px.line(
                    chart_df,
                    x=x,
                    y=y,
                    markers=True
                )

            elif chart_type == "pie":

                fig = px.pie(
                    chart_df,
                    names=x,
                    values=y,
                    hole=0.35
                )

            elif chart_type == "scatter":

                fig = px.scatter(
                    chart_df,
                    x=x,
                    y=y,
                    trendline="ols"
                )

            elif chart_type == "histogram":

                fig = px.histogram(
                    chart_df,
                    x=x,
                    nbins=20
                )

            else:

                return False

            fig.update_layout(
                height=450,
                margin=dict(
                    l=20,
                    r=20,
                    t=50,
                    b=50
                ),
                template="plotly_dark",
                hovermode="closest"
            )

            st.plotly_chart(
                fig,
                use_container_width=True,
                config={
                    "displayModeBar": False
                }
            )

            return True

        except Exception:
            pass

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # STREAMLIT FALLBACK
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    try:

        if chart_type == "bar":

            st.bar_chart(
                chart_df.set_index(x)[y]
                if x and y
                else chart_df,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        if chart_type == "line":

            st.line_chart(
                chart_df.set_index(x)[y]
                if x and y
                else chart_df,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        if chart_type == "scatter":

            st.scatter_chart(
                chart_df,
                x=x,
                y=y,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        if chart_type == "histogram":

            st.bar_chart(
                chart_df,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

    except Exception:
        pass

    return False

def show_comparison(

    question,
    dimension,
    metric
):

    values = mentioned_values(

        question
    )

    if len(values) < 2:
        return False

    selected = values[:2]

    aggregation = determine_aggregation(
        question
    )

    grouped = aggregate_grouped(
        df,
        dimension,
        metric,
        aggregation
    )

    if grouped.empty:
        return False

    comparison = (
        grouped
        .reindex(selected)
        .dropna()
    )

    if len(comparison) != 2:
        return False

    label = (
        "Average"
        if aggregation == "mean"
        else "Total"
    )

    # Explicit dataframe prevents unwanted categories
    chart_df = (
        comparison
        .rename("Value")
        .reset_index()
    )

    chart_df.columns = [
        dimension,
        "Value"
    ]

    render_chart(
        chart_df,
        "bar",
        f"{selected[0]} vs {selected[1]}",
        dimension,
        "Value"
    )

    show_result_table(
        comparison,
        dimension,
        f"{label} {metric}"
    )

    first = float(
        comparison.iloc[0]
    )

    second = float(
        comparison.iloc[1]
    )

    difference = abs(
        first - second
    )

    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)

    with col1:

        st.metric(
            "Difference",
            f"{difference:,.2f}"
        )

    with col2:

        if first > second:
            higher = selected[0]

        elif second > first:
            higher = selected[1]

        else:
            higher = "Equal"

        st.metric(
            "Higher",
            higher
        )

    if first > second:

        st.success(
            f"{selected[0]} has higher "
            f"{label.lower()} {metric.lower()} "
            f"than {selected[1]}."
        )

    elif second > first:

        st.success(
            f"{selected[1]} has higher "
            f"{label.lower()} {metric.lower()} "
            f"than {selected[0]}."
        )

    else:

        st.info(
            f"{selected[0]} and {selected[1]} "
            f"have equal {label.lower()} "
            f"{metric.lower()}."
        )

    return True
```
