import re
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st


# =========================================================
# NORMALIZATION
# =========================================================

def _normalize(value):
    return re.sub(
        r"\s+",
        " ",
        str(value).strip().lower()
    )


def _clean_columns(df):
    df = df.copy()

    df.columns = [
        str(column).strip()
        for column in df.columns
    ]

    return df


# =========================================================
# COLUMN DETECTION
# =========================================================

def _find_column(df, candidates):
    """
    Find a dataset column using exact and partial matching.
    """

    normalized = {
        _normalize(column)
        .replace(" ", "")
        .replace("_", ""): column
        for column in df.columns
    }

    # Exact match
    for candidate in candidates:

        key = (
            _normalize(candidate)
            .replace(" ", "")
            .replace("_", "")
        )

        if key in normalized:
            return normalized[key]

    # Partial match
    for column in df.columns:

        column_key = (
            _normalize(column)
            .replace(" ", "")
            .replace("_", "")
        )

        for candidate in candidates:

            candidate_key = (
                _normalize(candidate)
                .replace(" ", "")
                .replace("_", "")
            )

            if (
                candidate_key
                and candidate_key in column_key
            ):
                return column

    return None


def _numeric_columns(df):
    return (
        df
        .select_dtypes(include="number")
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )


def _categorical_columns(df):
    return (
        df
        .select_dtypes(
            include=[
                "object",
                "category",
                "string"
            ]
        )
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )


# =========================================================
# QUESTION WORD DETECTION
# =========================================================

def _comparison_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    patterns = [
        r"\bcompare\b",
        r"\bcomparison\b",
        r"\bversus\b",
        r"\bvs\b",
        r"\bdifference between\b",
        r"\bcompare between\b",
    ]

    return any(
        re.search(pattern, q)
        for pattern in patterns
    )


def _average_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "average",
            "avg",
            "mean",
        ]
    )


def _total_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "total",
            "sum",
            "overall",
        ]
    )


def _highest_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "highest",
            "maximum",
            "max",
            "top",
            "most",
            "best",
        ]
    )


def _lowest_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "lowest",
            "minimum",
            "min",
            "least",
            "worst",
            "smallest",
        ]
    )


# =========================================================
# CHART INTENT DETECTION
# =========================================================

def _is_time_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "trend",
            "over time",
            "by month",
            "per month",
            "monthly",
            "month",
            "by year",
            "per year",
            "yearly",
            "year",
            "by day",
            "per day",
            "daily",
            "date",
            "dates",
            "timeline",
        ]
    )


def _is_distribution_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "distribution",
            "spread",
            "frequency",
            "histogram",
            "distribute",
        ]
    )


def _is_relationship_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "relationship",
            "correlation",
            "correlated",
            "relationship between",
            "relation between",
            "against",
        ]
    )


def _is_share_question(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in [
            "share",
            "percentage",
            "percent",
            "proportion",
            "contribution",
            "contribute",
            "breakdown",
        ]
    )


# =========================================================
# NUMERIC CONVERSION
# =========================================================

def _numeric(df, column):

    return pd.to_numeric(
        df[column],
        errors="coerce"
    )


# =========================================================
# FIND METRIC MENTIONED IN QUESTION
# =========================================================

def _find_metric_column(df, question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    numeric_columns = _numeric_columns(df)

    if not numeric_columns:
        return None

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Exact / partial column-name matching
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    for column in numeric_columns:

        column_text = _normalize(column)

        variants = [
            column_text,
            column_text.replace("_", " "),
            column_text.replace("_", ""),
        ]

        for variant in variants:

            if variant and variant in q:
                return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Common business metric aliases
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    aliases = {

        "sales": [
            "sales",
            "revenue",
            "turnover",
        ],

        "revenue": [
            "revenue",
            "sales",
            "turnover",
        ],

        "salary": [
            "salary",
            "salaries",
            "pay",
            "wage",
            "income",
            "compensation",
        ],

        "quantity": [
            "quantity",
            "units",
            "volume",
        ],

        "profit": [
            "profit",
            "profits",
            "margin",
        ],

        "performance": [
            "performance",
            "score",
            "rating",
        ],

        "experience": [
            "experience",
            "years",
            "tenure",
        ],

        "age": [
            "age",
        ],
    }

    for column in numeric_columns:

        column_text = _normalize(column)

        for key, words in aliases.items():

            if key in column_text:

                if any(
                    word in q
                    for word in words
                ):
                    return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # One numeric column = safest fallback
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if len(numeric_columns) == 1:
        return numeric_columns[0]

    return None


# =========================================================
# FIND DIMENSION COLUMN
# =========================================================

def _find_dimension_column(
    df,
    question,
    mentioned_values=None
):

    categorical_columns = _categorical_columns(df)

    if not categorical_columns:
        return None

    q = _normalize(question)

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Explicit column name
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    for column in categorical_columns:

        column_text = _normalize(column)

        variants = [
            column_text,
            column_text.replace("_", " "),
            column_text.replace("_", ""),
        ]

        if any(
            variant
            and variant in q
            for variant in variants
        ):
            return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Value-based detection
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if mentioned_values:

        for column in categorical_columns:

            values = (
                df[column]
                .dropna()
                .astype(str)
                .str.strip()
                .unique()
                .tolist()
            )

            normalized_values = {
                _normalize(value)
                for value in values
            }

            matches = 0

            for value in mentioned_values:

                if (
                    _normalize(value)
                    in normalized_values
                ):
                    matches += 1

            if matches >= 2:
                return column

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Common dimensions
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    dimension_words = [
        "department",
        "dept",
        "region",
        "area",
        "location",
        "city",
        "state",
        "country",
        "category",
        "segment",
        "product",
        "team",
        "division",
        "gender",
        "customer",
        "employee",
        "name",
    ]

    for column in categorical_columns:

        column_text = (
            _normalize(column)
            .replace("_", " ")
        )

        if any(
            word in column_text
            for word in dimension_words
        ):

            if any(
                word in q
                for word in dimension_words
            ):
                return column

    return None


# =========================================================
# FIND VALUES MENTIONED IN QUESTION
# =========================================================

def _mentioned_values(
    df,
    column,
    question
):

    question_text = _normalize(question)

    values = (
        df[column]
        .dropna()
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
        .unique()
        .tolist()
    )

    matches = []

    for value in values:

        value_text = _normalize(value)

        if not value_text:
            continue

        pattern = (
            r"(?<!\w)"
            + re.escape(value_text)
            + r"(?!\w)"
        )

        match = re.search(
            pattern,
            question_text
        )

        if match:

            matches.append(
                (
                    match.start(),
                    value
                )
            )

    matches.sort(
        key=lambda item: item[0]
    )

    result = []
    seen = set()

    for _, value in matches:

        key = _normalize(value)

        if key not in seen:

            seen.add(key)
            result.append(value)

    return result


# =========================================================
# CHART RENDERER
# =========================================================

def _render_chart(
    data,
    chart_type,
    title=None,
    dimension_col=None,
    metric_col=None
):
    """
    Central chart rendering function.

    Supported:
        bar
        line
        pie
        scatter
        histogram
    """

    if data is None or data.empty:
        return False

    if title:
        st.markdown(
            f"### 📊 {title}"
        )

    # =====================================================
    # BAR
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "bar":

        st.bar_chart(
            data,
            use_container_width=True
        )

        return True

    # =====================================================
    # LINE
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "line":

        st.line_chart(
            data,
            use_container_width=True
        )

        return True

    # =====================================================
    # SCATTER
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "scatter":

        try:

            import plotly.express as px

            if (
                dimension_col is None
                or metric_col is None
            ):
                return False

            plot_data = data.copy()

            fig = px.scatter(
                plot_data,
                x=dimension_col,
                y=metric_col,
                title=None,
            )

            fig.update_layout(
                margin=dict(
                    l=20,
                    r=20,
                    t=20,
                    b=20
                )
            )

            st.plotly_chart(
                fig,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        except Exception:

            # Graceful fallback
            st.scatter_chart(
                data,
                x=dimension_col,
                y=metric_col,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

    # =====================================================
    # PIE
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "pie":

        try:

            import plotly.express as px

            if (
                dimension_col is None
                or metric_col is None
            ):
                return False

            plot_data = data.copy()

            fig = px.pie(
                plot_data,
                names=dimension_col,
                values=metric_col,
            )

            fig.update_layout(
                margin=dict(
                    l=20,
                    r=20,
                    t=20,
                    b=20
                )
            )

            st.plotly_chart(
                fig,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        except Exception:

            # If Plotly isn't installed,
            # use a bar chart instead.
            st.bar_chart(
                data.set_index(
                    dimension_col
                )[metric_col],
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

    # =====================================================
    # HISTOGRAM
    # =====================================================

    if chart_type == "histogram":

        try:

            import plotly.express as px

            plot_data = data.copy()

            fig = px.histogram(
                plot_data,
                x=metric_col,
                nbins=20,
            )

            fig.update_layout(
                margin=dict(
                    l=20,
                    r=20,
                    t=20,
                    b=20
                )
            )

            st.plotly_chart(
                fig,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

        except Exception:

            # Fallback histogram using
            # pandas value counts.

            histogram = (
                data[metric_col]
                .dropna()
                .value_counts()
                .sort_index()
            )

            st.bar_chart(
                histogram,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            return True

    return False


# =========================================================
# INTELLIGENT CHART SELECTION
# =========================================================

def _choose_chart_type(
    question,
    dimension_col=None,
    metric_col=None,
    df=None
):
    """
    Decide the most appropriate chart based
    on the question and dataset structure.
    """

    q = _normalize(question)

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Distribution
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if _is_distribution_question(question):

        return "histogram"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Relationship / correlation
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if _is_relationship_question(question):

        if (
            df is not None
            and len(_numeric_columns(df)) >= 2
        ):
            return "scatter"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Time / trend
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if _is_time_question(question):

        return "line"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Share / percentage
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if _is_share_question(question):

        return "pie"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Comparison
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if _comparison_requested(question):

        return "bar"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Highest / lowest / top
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if (
        _highest_requested(question)
        or _lowest_requested(question)
    ):

        return "bar"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Grouped categorical analysis
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if (
        dimension_col is not None
        and metric_col is not None
    ):

        return "bar"

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Default
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    return "bar"


# =========================================================
# GENERIC GROUPED VISUALIZATION
# =========================================================

def _show_grouped(
    df,
    dimension_col,
    metric_col,
    aggregation,
    title,
    question=None
):

    data = df.copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            dimension_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    if data.empty:
        return False

    if aggregation == "mean":

        grouped = (
            data
            .groupby(dimension_col)[metric_col]
            .mean()
        )

        label = "Average"

    elif aggregation == "count":

        grouped = (
            data
            .groupby(dimension_col)[metric_col]
            .count()
        )

        label = "Count"

    else:

        grouped = (
            data
            .groupby(dimension_col)[metric_col]
            .sum()
        )

        label = "Total"

    grouped = (
        grouped
        .sort_values(
            ascending=False
        )
        .head(20)
    )

    if grouped.empty:
        return False

    chart_type = _choose_chart_type(
        question or "",
        dimension_col,
        metric_col,
        df
    )

    # Pie needs a dataframe with explicit columns
    if chart_type == "pie":

        chart_data = (
            grouped
            .reset_index()
        )

        _render_chart(
            chart_data,
            "pie",
            title,
            dimension_col,
            metric_col
        )

    elif chart_type == "line":

        chart_data = (
            grouped
            .rename(
                f"{label} {metric_col}"
            )
            .to_frame()
        )

        _render_chart(
            chart_data,
            "line",
            title,
            dimension_col,
            metric_col
        )

    else:

        chart_data = (
            grouped
            .rename(
                f"{label} {metric_col}"
            )
        )

        _render_chart(
            chart_data,
            "bar",
            title,
            dimension_col,
            metric_col
        )

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Table
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    table = (
        grouped
        .rename("Value")
        .reset_index()
    )

    st.dataframe(
        table,
        use_container_width=True,
        hide_index=True
    )

    return True


# =========================================================
# GENERIC COMPARISON
# =========================================================

def _show_generic_comparison(
    df,
    question,
    dimension_col,
    metric_col
):

    values = _mentioned_values(
        df,
        dimension_col,
        question
    )

    if len(values) < 2:
        return False

    selected = values[:2]

    data = df.copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data["__dimension__"] = (
        data[dimension_col]
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    data = data[
        data["__dimension__"].isin(
            selected
        )
    ]

    if data.empty:
        return False

    q = _normalize(question)

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Aggregation
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if (
        "average" in q
        or "avg" in q
        or "mean" in q
    ):

        grouped = (
            data
            .groupby("__dimension__")[metric_col]
            .mean()
        )

        aggregation_label = "Average"

    elif (
        "total" in q
        or "sum" in q
    ):

        grouped = (
            data
            .groupby("__dimension__")[metric_col]
            .sum()
        )

        aggregation_label = "Total"

    else:

        # Default comparison = TOTAL
        grouped = (
            data
            .groupby("__dimension__")[metric_col]
            .sum()
        )

        aggregation_label = "Total"

    grouped = grouped.reindex(
        selected
    )

    if grouped.isna().any():
        return False

    first_value = float(
        grouped.iloc[0]
    )

    second_value = float(
        grouped.iloc[1]
    )

    difference = abs(
        first_value - second_value
    )

    first_name = selected[0]
    second_name = selected[1]

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Chart
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    chart_data = (
        grouped
        .rename(
            f"{aggregation_label} {metric_col}"
        )
    )

    _render_chart(
        chart_data,
        "bar",
        f"{first_name} vs {second_name} — "
        f"{aggregation_label} {metric_col}",
        dimension_col,
        metric_col
    )

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Table
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    table = (
        grouped
        .rename(
            f"{aggregation_label} {metric_col}"
        )
        .reset_index()
    )

    table.columns = [
        dimension_col,
        f"{aggregation_label} {metric_col}"
    ]

    st.dataframe(
        table,
        use_container_width=True,
        hide_index=True
    )

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Difference
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)

    with col1:

        st.metric(
            "Difference",
            f"{difference:,.2f}"
        )

    with col2:

        if first_value > second_value:
            higher = first_name

        elif second_value > first_value:
            higher = second_name

        else:
            higher = "Equal"

        st.metric(
            "Higher",
            higher
        )

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Explanation
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    if first_value > second_value:

        st.info(
            f"{first_name} has higher "
            f"{aggregation_label.lower()} "
            f"{metric_col} than "
            f"{second_name}."
        )

    elif second_value > first_value:

        st.info(
            f"{second_name} has higher "
            f"{aggregation_label.lower()} "
            f"{metric_col} than "
            f"{first_name}."
        )

    else:

        st.info(
            f"{first_name} and "
            f"{second_name} have equal "
            f"{aggregation_label.lower()} "
            f"{metric_col}."
        )

    return True


# =========================================================
# PERSON RANKING
# =========================================================

def _show_top_employee(
    df,
    question,
    person_col,
    metric_col,
    descending=True
):

    if descending:

        ranking_requested = _highest_requested(
            question
        )

    else:

        ranking_requested = _lowest_requested(
            question
        )

    if not ranking_requested:
        return False

    data = df[
        [
            person_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    ].copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            person_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    if data.empty:
        return False

    grouped = (
        data
        .groupby(person_col)[metric_col]
        .mean()
        .sort_values(
            ascending=not descending
        )
    )

    if grouped.empty:
        return False

    q = _normalize(question)

    limit_match = re.search(
        r"\btop\s+(\d+)\b",
        q
    )

    limit = (
        int(limit_match.group(1))
        if limit_match
        else 1
    )

    result = grouped.head(
        limit
    )

    if descending:

        title = (
            f"Top {limit}"
            if limit > 1
            else "Highest"
        )

    else:

        title = "Lowest"

    chart_data = result.rename(
        metric_col
    )

    _render_chart(
        chart_data,
        "bar",
        f"{title} {metric_col}",
        person_col,
        metric_col
    )

    table = (
        result
        .rename(metric_col)
        .reset_index()
    )

    st.dataframe(
        table,
        use_container_width=True,
        hide_index=True
    )

    return True


# =========================================================
# THRESHOLD ANALYSIS
# =========================================================

def _show_threshold(
    df,
    question,
    person_col,
    metric_col
):

    q = _normalize(question)

    patterns = [

        (
            r"(?:more than|greater than|above|over|exceeding)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            ">"
        ),

        (
            r"(?:less than|below|under)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            "<"
        ),

        (
            r"(?:at least|minimum of)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            ">="
        ),

        (
            r"(?:at most|maximum of)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            "<="
        ),
    ]

    operator = None
    threshold = None

    for pattern, op in patterns:

        match = re.search(
            pattern,
            q
        )

        if match:

            threshold = float(
                match.group(1)
                .replace(",", "")
            )

            operator = op

            break

    if operator is None:
        return False

    data = df[
        [
            person_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    ].copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            person_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    if operator == ">":

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] > threshold
        ]

    elif operator == "<":

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] < threshold
        ]

    elif operator == ">=":

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] >= threshold
        ]

    else:

        result = data[
            data[metric_col] <= threshold
        ]

    result = result.sort_values(
        metric_col,
        ascending=False
    )

    st.markdown(
        f"### 📊 {metric_col} "
        f"{operator} "
        f"{threshold:,.0f}"
    )

    if result.empty:

        st.info(
            "No matching records were found."
        )

    else:

        st.dataframe(
            result,
            use_container_width=True,
            hide_index=True
        )

        chart_data = (
            result
            .set_index(person_col)[
                metric_col
            ]
        )

        _render_chart(

        )

    return True

```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import re


# =========================================================
# HELPER
# =========================================================

def _numeric_series(df, column):
    """Safely convert a column to numeric."""
    return pd.to_numeric(
        df[column],
        errors="coerce"
    )


# =========================================================
# MAIN VISUAL ANALYSIS
# =========================================================

def generate_visual_analysis(df, question=None):
    """
    Generate a visualization based on the user's question.

    Supports:
        - Salary analysis
        - Salary thresholds
        - Performance analysis
        - Experience analysis
        - Department average salary
        - Department total salary
        - Department comparisons
        - Generic visual analysis

    Returns:
        True  -> visualization generated
        False -> no suitable visualization
    """

    if df is None or df.empty:
        return False

    df = df.copy()

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # CLEAN COLUMN NAMES
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    df.columns = [
        str(column).strip()
        for column in df.columns
    ]

    question_lower = (
        question.lower().strip()
        if question
        else ""
    )

    chart_created = False

    # =====================================================
    # DETECT EMPLOYEE DATASET COLUMNS
    # =====================================================

    has_employee = "Employee" in df.columns
    has_salary = "Salary" in df.columns
    has_performance = "Performance_Score" in df.columns
    has_experience = "Experience" in df.columns
    has_department = "Department" in df.columns

    # =====================================================
    # 1. SALARY QUESTIONS
    # =====================================================

    salary_question = (
        has_employee
        and has_salary
        and (
            "salary" in question_lower
            or "paid" in question_lower
            or "earn" in question_lower
            or "income" in question_lower
        )
    )

    if salary_question:

        salary_df = df[
            ["Employee", "Salary"]
        ].copy()

        salary_df["Salary"] = _numeric_series(
            salary_df,
            "Salary"
        )

        salary_df = salary_df.dropna(
            subset=["Salary"]
        )

        # -------------------------------------------------
        # THRESHOLD QUESTION
        # -------------------------------------------------

        threshold_match = re.search(
            r"(?:more than|greater than|above|over|exceeding)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+)",
            question_lower
        )

        if threshold_match:

            threshold_text = (
                threshold_match.group(1)
                .replace(",", "")
            )

            threshold = float(
                threshold_text
            )

            filtered = salary_df[
                salary_df["Salary"] > threshold
            ].copy()

            filtered = filtered.sort_values(
                "Salary",
                ascending=False
            )

            st.markdown(
                f"### 💰 Employees Earning More Than "
                f"{threshold:,.0f}"
            )

            if not filtered.empty:

                chart_data = (
                    filtered
                    .set_index("Employee")["Salary"]
                )

                st.bar_chart(
                    chart_data,
                    use_container_width=True
                )

                st.dataframe(
                    filtered,
                    use_container_width=True,
                    hide_index=True
                )

                chart_created = True

            else:

                st.info(
                    f"No employees earn more than "
                    f"{threshold:,.0f}."
                )

                chart_created = True

        # -------------------------------------------------
        # SPECIFIC EMPLOYEE SALARY
        # -------------------------------------------------

        elif (
            "what is" in question_lower
            or "salary of" in question_lower
            or "salary for" in question_lower
        ):

            salary_df = salary_df.sort_values(
                "Salary",
                ascending=False
            )

            st.markdown(
                "### 💰 Salary by Employee"
            )

            chart_data = (
                salary_df
                .set_index("Employee")["Salary"]
            )

            st.bar_chart(
                chart_data,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            st.dataframe(
                salary_df,
                use_container_width=True,
                hide_index=True
            )

            chart_created = True

        # -------------------------------------------------
        # HIGHEST / LOWEST SALARY
        # -------------------------------------------------

        else:

            ascending = (
                "lowest" in question_lower
                or "least paid" in question_lower
            )

            salary_df = salary_df.sort_values(
                "Salary",
                ascending=ascending
            )

            st.markdown(
                "### 💰 Salary by Employee"
            )

            chart_data = (
                salary_df
                .set_index("Employee")["Salary"]
            )

            st.bar_chart(
                chart_data,
                use_container_width=True
            )

            st.dataframe(
                salary_df,
                use_container_width=True,
                hide_index=True
            )

            chart_created = True

    # =====================================================
    # 2. PERFORMANCE QUESTIONS

    if (
        has_employee
        and has_performance
        and (
            "performance" in question_lower
            or "performance score" in question_lower
        )

            [
                "Employee",
                "Performance_Score"
            ]

        )

        chart_created = True

    # =====================================================

    # =====================================================

    if (
        has_department
        and has_salary
        and "department" in question_lower
        and "salary" in question_lower
        and (
```

import re
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st


def _normalize(value):
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(value).strip().lower())


def _find_column(df, candidates):
    normalized = {
        _normalize(c).replace(" ", ""): c
        for c in df.columns
    }

    # Exact normalized match first.
    for candidate in candidates:
        key = _normalize(candidate).replace(" ", "")
        if key in normalized:
            return normalized[key]

    # Then partial match.
    for column in df.columns:
        key = _normalize(column).replace(" ", "")

        for candidate in candidates:
            candidate_key = _normalize(candidate).replace(" ", "")

            if candidate_key and candidate_key in key:
                return column

    return None


def _numeric(df, column):
    return pd.to_numeric(df[column], errors="coerce")


def _mentioned_values(df, column, question):
    """
    Return dataset values explicitly mentioned in the question,
    in question order.
    """

    question_text = _normalize(question)

    values = [
        value
        for value in (
            df[column]
            .dropna()
            .astype(str)
            .str.strip()
            .unique()
            .tolist()
        )
        if value
    ]

    matches = []

    for value in values:
        value_text = _normalize(value)

        if not value_text:
            continue

        pattern = (
            r"(?<!\w)"
            + re.escape(value_text)
            + r"(?!\w)"
        )

        match = re.search(pattern, question_text)

        if match:
            matches.append((match.start(), value))

    matches.sort(key=lambda item: item[0])

    result = []
    seen = set()

    for _, value in matches:
        key = _normalize(value)

        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            result.append(value)

    return result


def _comparison_requested(question):
    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        phrase in q
        for phrase in (
            "compare",
            "comparison",
            "versus",
            " vs ",
            "difference between",
            "compare between",
        )
    )


def _show_comparison(
    df,
    question,
    department_col,
    metric_col,
    metric_label
):
    departments = _mentioned_values(
        df,
        department_col,
        question
    )

    if len(departments) < 2:
        return False

    selected = departments[:2]

    working = df.copy()

    working[metric_col] = _numeric(
        working,
        metric_col
    )

    working["__dimension__"] = (
        working[department_col]
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
    )

    grouped = (
        working[
            working["__dimension__"].isin(selected)
        ]
        .dropna(subset=[metric_col])
        .groupby("__dimension__")[metric_col]
        .mean()
        .reindex(selected)
    )

    if grouped.isna().any() or len(grouped) != 2:
        return False

    first = selected[0]
    second = selected[1]

    first_value = float(
        grouped.loc[first]
    )

    second_value = float(
        grouped.loc[second]
    )

    difference = abs(
        first_value - second_value
    )

    st.markdown(
        f"### 📊 {first} vs {second} — "
        f"Average {metric_label}"
    )

    st.bar_chart(
        grouped.rename(
            f"Average {metric_label}"
        ),
        use_container_width=True
    )

    table = (
        grouped
        .rename(
            f"Average {metric_label}"
        )
        .reset_index()
    )

    table.columns = [
        department_col,
        f"Average {metric_label}"
    ]

    st.dataframe(
        table,
        use_container_width=True,
        hide_index=True
    )

    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)

    with col1:
        st.metric(
            f"{metric_label} Difference",
            f"{difference:,.0f}"
        )

    with col2:
        if first_value > second_value:
            higher = first

        elif second_value > first_value:
            higher = second

        else:
            higher = "Equal"

        st.metric(
            f"Higher Average {metric_label}",
            higher
        )

    return True


def _show_top_employee(
    df,
    question,
    person_col,
    metric_col,
    metric_label,
    descending=True
):
    q = _normalize(question)

    if descending:
        ranking_words = (
            "highest",
            "top",
            "most",
            "maximum",
            "max",
            "best",
        )
    else:
        ranking_words = (
            "lowest",
            "least",
            "minimum",
            "min",
            "worst",
            "smallest",
        )

    if not any(
        word in q
        for word in ranking_words
    ):
        return False

    data = df[
        [person_col, metric_col]
    ].copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            person_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    if data.empty:
        return False

    grouped = (
        data
        .groupby(person_col)[metric_col]
        .mean()
        .sort_values(
            ascending=not descending
        )
    )

    if grouped.empty:
        return False

    limit_match = re.search(
        r"\btop\s+(\d+)\b",
        q
    )

    limit = (
        int(limit_match.group(1))
        if limit_match
        else 1
    )

    result = grouped.head(limit)

    if descending and limit > 1:
        title = f"Top {limit}"

    elif descending:
        title = "Highest"

    else:
        title = "Lowest"

    st.markdown(
        f"### 📊 {title} {metric_label}"
    )

    st.bar_chart(
        result.rename(metric_label),
        use_container_width=True
    )

    table = (
        result
        .rename(metric_label)
        .reset_index()
    )

    st.dataframe(
        table,
        use_container_width=True,
        hide_index=True
    )

    return True


def _show_threshold(
    df,
    question,
    person_col,
    metric_col,
    metric_label
):
    q = _normalize(question)

    patterns = [
        (
            r"(?:more than|greater than|above|over|exceeding)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            ">"
        ),
        (
            r"(?:less than|below|under)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            "<"
        ),
        (
            r"(?:at least|minimum of)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            ">="
        ),
        (
            r"(?:at most|maximum of)"
            r"\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)",
            "<="
        ),
    ]

    operator = None
    threshold = None

    for pattern, op in patterns:

        match = re.search(
            pattern,
            q
        )

        if match:
            threshold = float(
                match.group(1).replace(",", "")
            )

            operator = op
            break

    if operator is None:
        return False

    data = df[
        [person_col, metric_col]
    ].copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            person_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    if operator == ">":
        result = data[
            data[metric_col] > threshold
        ]

    elif operator == "<":
        result = data[
            data[metric_col] < threshold
        ]

    elif operator == ">=":
        result = data[
            data[metric_col] >= threshold
        ]

    else:
        result = data[
            data[metric_col] <= threshold
        ]

    result = result.sort_values(
        metric_col,
        ascending=False
    )

    st.markdown(
        f"### 📊 Employees "
        f"{operator} "
        f"{threshold:,.0f} "
        f"{metric_label}"
    )

    if result.empty:

        st.info(
            "No matching employees were found."
        )

    else:

        st.dataframe(
            result,
            use_container_width=True,
            hide_index=True
        )

        st.bar_chart(
            result.set_index(person_col)[
                metric_col
            ],
            use_container_width=True
        )

    return True


def _show_grouped(
    df,
    dimension_col,
    metric_col,
    aggregation,
    title
):
    data = df.copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            dimension_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    if data.empty:
        return False

    if aggregation == "mean":

        grouped = (
            data
            .groupby(dimension_col)[metric_col]
            .mean()
        )

        label = "Average"

    else:

        grouped = (
            data
            .groupby(dimension_col)[metric_col]
            .sum()
        )

        label = "Total"

    grouped = (
        grouped
        .sort_values(
            ascending=False
        )
        .head(20)
    )

    if grouped.empty:
        return False

    st.markdown(
        f"### 📊 {title}"
    )

    st.bar_chart(
        grouped.rename(
            f"{label} {metric_col}"
        ),
        use_container_width=True
    )

    table = (
        grouped
        .rename("Value")
        .reset_index()
    )

    st.dataframe(
        table,
        use_container_width=True,
        hide_index=True
    )

    return True


def _show_highest_group_average(
    df,
    dimension_col,
    metric_col,
    metric_label
):
    """
    Show average metric by group and identify
    the group with the highest average.
    """

    data = df.copy()

    data[metric_col] = _numeric(
        data,
        metric_col
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=[
            dimension_col,
            metric_col
        ]
    )

    if data.empty:
        return False

    grouped = (
        data
        .groupby(dimension_col)[metric_col]
        .mean()
        .sort_values(
            ascending=False
        )
    )

    if grouped.empty:
        return False

    highest_dimension = grouped.index[0]

    highest_value = float(
        grouped.iloc[0]
    )

    st.markdown(
        f"### 📊 Highest Average "
        f"{metric_label} by "
        f"{dimension_col}"
    )

    # Show all department averages.
    st.bar_chart(
        grouped.rename(
            f"Average {metric_label}"
        ),
        use_container_width=True
    )

    table = (
        grouped
        .rename(
            f"Average {metric_label}"
        )
        .reset_index()
    )

    st.dataframe(
        table,
        use_container_width=True,
        hide_index=True
    )

    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)

    with col1:
        st.metric(
            f"Highest Average {metric_label}",
            f"{highest_value:,.0f}"
        )

    with col2:
        st.metric(
            "Department",
            str(highest_dimension)
        )

    st.success(
        f"{highest_dimension} has the highest "
        f"average {metric_label.lower()} "
        f"at {highest_value:,.0f}."
    )

    return True


def generate_visual_analysis(
    df,
    question=None
):
    """
    Generate one question-specific visualization
    and return True when successful.
    """

    if df is None or df.empty or not question:
        return False

    data = df.copy()

    data.columns = [
        str(column).strip()
        for column in data.columns
    ]

    q = _normalize(question)

    department_col = _find_column(
        data,
        [
            "Department",
            "Dept",
            "Team",
            "Division",
        ]
    )

    person_col = _find_column(
        data,
        [
            "Employee",
            "Employee_Name",
            "Employee Name",
            "Name",
            "Person",
            "Staff",
        ]
    )

    salary_col = _find_column(
        data,
        [
            "Salary",
            "Salaries",
            "Pay",
            "Wage",
            "Compensation",
            "Income",
        ]
    )

    performance_col = _find_column(
        data,
        [
            "Performance_Score",
            "Performance Score",
            "Performance",
            "Score",
            "Rating",
        ]
    )

    experience_col = _find_column(
        data,
        [
            "Experience",
            "Years_Experience",
            "Years Experience",
            "Years",
            "Tenure",
        ]
    )

    # =========================================================
    # 1. DEPARTMENT / GROUP COMPARISON
    # =========================================================

    # Comparison is deliberately handled first so it cannot
    # fall through to a generic salary visualization.
    if (
        _comparison_requested(question)
        and department_col
    ):

        # Salary comparison.
        if (
            salary_col
            and any(
                word in q
                for word in (
                    "salary",
                    "salaries",
                    "paid",
                    "pay",
                    "earn",
                    "income",
                )
            )
        ):

            if _show_comparison(
                data,
                question,
                department_col,
                salary_col,
                "Salary",
            ):
                return True

        # Performance comparison.
        if (
            performance_col
            and any(
                word in q
                for word in (
                    "performance",
                    "performing",
                    "score",
                    "scores",
                    "rating",
                    "ratings",
                )
            )
        ):

            if _show_comparison(
                data,
                question,
                department_col,
                performance_col,
                "Performance",
            ):
                return True

        # Experience comparison.
        if (
            experience_col
            and any(
                word in q
                for word in (
                    "experience",
                    "experienced",
                    "years",
                    "tenure",
                )
            )
        ):

            if _show_comparison(
                data,
                question,
                department_col,
                experience_col,
                "Experience",
            ):
                return True

    # =========================================================
    # 2. HIGHEST AVERAGE SALARY BY DEPARTMENT
    # =========================================================

    # IMPORTANT:
    # This must come BEFORE person-specific ranking.
    #
    # Otherwise:
    #
    # "Which department has the highest average salary?"
    #
    # could be incorrectly interpreted as:
    #
    # "Who has the highest salary?"
    #
    if (
        department_col
        and salary_col
        and (
            "average" in q
            or "mean" in q
            or "avg" in q
        )
        and any(
            word in q
            for word in (
                "highest",
                "maximum",
                "max",
                "top",
            )
        )
        and any(
            word in q
            for word in (
                "department",
                "dept",
                "team",
                "division",
            )
        )
    ):

        if _show_highest_group_average(
            data,
            department_col,
            salary_col,
            "Salary",
        ):
            return True

    # =========================================================
    # 3. PERSON-SPECIFIC / RANKING VISUALIZATIONS
    # =========================================================

    # Salary ranking.
    if (
        person_col
        and salary_col
        and any(
            word in q
            for word in (
                "salary",
                "salaries",
                "paid",
                "pay",
                "earn",
                "income",
            )
        )
    ):

        # Salary threshold.
        if _show_threshold(
            data,
            question,
            person_col,
            salary_col,
            "salary",
        ):
            return True

        # Highest salary.
        if _show_top_employee(
            data,
            question,
            person_col,
            salary_col,
            "Salary",
            descending=True,
        ):
            return True

        # Lowest salary.
        if _show_top_employee(
            data,
            question,
            person_col,
            salary_col,
            "Salary",
            descending=False,
        ):
            return True

    # Performance ranking.
    if (
        person_col
        and performance_col
        and any(
            word in q
            for word in (
                "performance",
                "performing",
                "score",
                "scores",
                "rating",
                "ratings",
            )
        )
    ):

        # Highest performance.
        if _show_top_employee(
            data,
            question,
            person_col,
            performance_col,
            "Performance",
            descending=True,
        ):
            return True

        # Lowest performance.
        if _show_top_employee(
            data,
            question,
            person_col,
            performance_col,
            "Performance",
            descending=False,
        ):
            return True

    # Experience ranking.
    if (
        person_col
        and experience_col
        and any(
            word in q
            for word in (
                "experience",
                "experienced",
                "years",
                "tenure",
            )
        )
    ):

        # Highest experience.
        if _show_top_employee(
            data,
            question,
            person_col,
            experience_col,
            "Experience",
            descending=True,
        ):
            return True

        # Lowest experience.
        if _show_top_employee(
            data,
            question,
            person_col,
            experience_col,
            "Experience",
            descending=False,
        ):
            return True

    # =========================================================
    # 4. DEPARTMENT SALARY QUESTIONS
    # =========================================================

    if (
        department_col
        and salary_col
        and "salary" in q
    ):

        # Average salary by department.
        if (
            "average" in q
            or "mean" in q
            or "avg" in q
        ):

            return _show_grouped(
                data,
                department_col,
                salary_col,
                "mean",
                "Average Salary by Department",
            )

        # Total salary by department.
        if (
            "total" in q
            or "sum" in q
        ):

            return _show_grouped(
                data,
                department_col,
                salary_col,
                "sum",
                "Total Salary by Department",
            )

    # =========================================================
    # 5. GENERIC CATEGORY VS NUMERIC FALLBACK
    # =========================================================

    numeric_columns = (
        data
        .select_dtypes(
            include="number"
        )
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )

    categorical_columns = (
        data
        .select_dtypes(
            include=[
                "object",
                "category",
            ]
        )
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )

    if (
        categorical_columns
        and numeric_columns
    ):

        dimension = categorical_columns[0]
        metric = numeric_columns[0]

        # Generic average.
        if any(
            word in q
            for word in (
                "average",
                "mean",
                "avg",
            )
        ):

            return _show_grouped(
                data,
                dimension,
                metric,
                "mean",
                f"Average {metric} by {dimension}",
            )

        # Generic total.
        if any(
            word in q
            for word in (
                "total",
                "sum",
            )
        ):

            return _show_grouped(
                data,
                dimension,
                metric,
                "sum",
                f"Total {metric} by {dimension}",
            )

    return False

We want Ollama to understand that:

- `SUM` → **total**
- `MEAN` → **average**
- `COUNT` → **count**
- It must **not infer the aggregation from previous conversation**.

### 1. Open `app.py`

Find the prompt inside **Ask Your Data**. You currently have something like:

```python
prompt = f"""
You are a professional business analyst.

You are answering a user who is having a conversation about a dataset.

PREVIOUS CONVERSATION:
{conversation_context}

CURRENT VERIFIED DATA:
{verified_result}

CURRENT USER QUESTION:
{user_question}

Rules:
...
"""
```

### 2. Replace the entire prompt with this

```python
prompt = f"""
You are a professional business analyst.

Your job is to explain the CURRENT VERIFIED DATA
in clear, natural language.

CURRENT USER QUESTION:
{user_question}

CURRENT VERIFIED DATA:
{verified_result}

PREVIOUS CONVERSATION:
{conversation_context}

IMPORTANT RULES:

1. The CURRENT VERIFIED DATA is the ONLY source of truth
   for the answer.

2. Do NOT recalculate anything yourself.

3. Do NOT change any number.

4. Do NOT change the meaning of the calculation.

5. Pay close attention to the aggregation used in the
   verified calculation.

6. If the verified calculation uses SUM, describe the
   result as:
   - total
   - total sales
   - total salary
   - total revenue
   as appropriate.

7. If the verified calculation uses MEAN or AVERAGE,
   describe the result as:
   - average
   - average salary
   - average sales
   - average score
   as appropriate.

8. If the verified calculation uses COUNT, describe the
   result as a count or number of records/items/employees.

9. NEVER call a SUM result an average.

10. NEVER call an AVERAGE result a total.

11. Previous conversation may only be used to understand
    references such as "it", "that", "this", or "the same".

12. Previous answers must NEVER override the current
    verified calculation.

13. Do not invent facts, numbers, trends, causes, or
    explanations that are not supported by the verified data.

14. Do not mention Python, Ollama, prompts, verified data,
    internal instructions, or the analysis engine.

15. Answer the user's CURRENT question directly.

16. Keep the answer concise and professional.
"""
```

### 3. Save

Press:

```text
Ctrl + S
```

Then restart:

```powershell
streamlit run app.py
```

Ask:

> **Which department has the highest salary?**

> **IT has the highest total salary, with $225,000.**

Then ask:

> **Which department has the highest average salary?**

We're making the architecture stricter:

```text
                CURRENT QUESTION
                       ↓
                question_parser
                       ↓

                       ↓
                Python calculation
                       ↓

                 ↙            ↘
              SUM             MEAN
```

This prevents the LLM from taking a correct `$225,000 SUM` and incorrectly calling it an **average** just because the previous question was about average salary.

import pandas as pd
import re

from question_parser import parse_question


# =========================================================
# HELPERS
# =========================================================

def normalize(text):
    """
    Normalize text for easier matching.
    Example:
    'Customer Segment' -> 'customersegment'
    """
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", str(text).lower())


def find_numeric_column(df, question):
    """
    Find the numeric column most relevant to the question.
    """

    numeric_columns = df.select_dtypes(
        include="number"
    ).columns.tolist()

    if not numeric_columns:
        return None

    question_lower = question.lower()
    question_normalized = normalize(question)

    aliases = {
        "sales": ["sales", "sale", "revenue", "income", "turnover"],
        "revenue": ["revenue", "sales", "income", "turnover"],
        "profit": ["profit", "earnings", "netprofit"],
        "salary": ["salary", "pay", "income", "wage"],
        "quantity": ["quantity", "units", "unit", "volume"],
        "amount": ["amount", "value", "price", "cost"],
        "cost": ["cost", "expense", "spend", "expenditure"],
        "spend": ["spend", "cost", "expense"],
        "clicks": ["clicks", "click"],
        "conversions": ["conversions", "conversion"],
        "score": ["score", "rating", "points"],
        "experience": ["experience", "years", "tenure"],
    }

    # Direct column-name matching
    for column in numeric_columns:

        normalized_column = normalize(column)

        if normalized_column in question_normalized:
            return column

    # Semantic matching
    for key, words in aliases.items():

        if key in question_lower:

            for column in numeric_columns:

                normalized_column = normalize(column)

                for word in words:

                    if normalize(word) in normalized_column:
                        return column

    # If only one numeric column exists
    if len(numeric_columns) == 1:
        return numeric_columns[0]

    # Common business metric priority
    priority = [
        "sales",
        "revenue",
        "profit",
        "amount",
        "salary",
        "quantity",
        "experience",
        "score",
        "cost",
        "price",
        "spend",
        "value"
    ]

    for priority_word in priority:

        for column in numeric_columns:

            if priority_word in normalize(column):
                return column

    return numeric_columns[0]


def find_dimension_column(df, question):
    """
    Find the categorical column most relevant to the question.
    """

    categorical_columns = df.select_dtypes(
        include=["object", "category"]
    ).columns.tolist()

    if not categorical_columns:
        return None

    question_normalized = normalize(question)
    question_lower = question.lower()

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Direct column-name matching
    # ---------------------------------------------------------

    for column in categorical_columns:

        column_normalized = normalize(column)

        if column_normalized in question_normalized:
            return column

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Semantic aliases
    # ---------------------------------------------------------

    aliases = {
        "product": ["product", "item", "model", "sku"],
        "region": [
            "region",
            "area",
            "location",
            "city",
            "state",
            "country"
        ],
        "customer": [
            "customer",
            "client",
            "buyer"
        ],
        "employee": [
            "employee",
            "staff",
            "worker"
        ],
        "department": [
            "department",
            "team",
            "division"
        ],
        "category": [
            "category",
            "type",
            "class"
        ],
        "campaign": [
            "campaign",
            "advertisement",
            "ad"
        ],
        "channel": [
            "channel",
            "source",
            "platform"
        ],
        "segment": [
            "segment",
            "group"
        ],
    }

    for key, words in aliases.items():

        if any(word in question_lower for word in words):

            for column in categorical_columns:

                column_normalized = normalize(column)

                for word in words:

                    if normalize(word) in column_normalized:
                        return column

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Detect category values mentioned in question
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # Example:
    # "Compare IT and Finance"
    #
    # Department column contains:
    # IT, Sales, HR, Finance
    #
    # Therefore Department should be selected.

    best_column = None
    best_match_count = 0

    for column in categorical_columns:

        match_count = 0

        for value in df[column].dropna().unique():

            value_normalized = normalize(value)

            if value_normalized and value_normalized in question_normalized:
                match_count += 1

        if match_count > best_match_count:

            best_match_count = match_count
            best_column = column

    if best_column is not None:
        return best_column

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. If only one categorical column exists
    # ---------------------------------------------------------

    if len(categorical_columns) == 1:
        return categorical_columns[0]

    return None


def find_category_values(df, dimension, question):
    """
    Find actual category values mentioned in the question.

    Example:
    Question:
        Compare IT and Finance

    Returns:
        ['IT', 'Finance']
    """

    question_normalized = normalize(question)

    matches = []

    for value in df[dimension].dropna().unique():

        if normalize(value) in question_normalized:

            matches.append(value)

    return matches


# =========================================================
# MAIN ANALYSIS ENGINE
# =========================================================

def analyze_dataset(df, question):
    """
    Dynamically analyze structured datasets.
    Python performs all calculations.
    Ollama only explains the calculated result.
    """

    question = question.lower().strip()

    intent = parse_question(question)

    numeric_columns = df.select_dtypes(
        include="number"
    ).columns.tolist()

    categorical_columns = df.select_dtypes(
        include=["object", "category"]
    ).columns.tolist()

    # =====================================================
    # 1. COMPARISON
    # =====================================================

    if intent["comparison"]:

        # Find the dimension directly from the question
        dimension = find_dimension_column(df, question)

        # If question contains IT / Finance, this should be Department
        if dimension:

            categories = find_category_values(
                df,
                dimension,
                question
            )

            if len(categories) >= 2:

                categories = categories[:2]

                # -----------------------------------------
                # Find metric

                metric = find_numeric_column(
                    df,

                )

                # If no metric is mentioned,
                # use Salary when available.
                if metric is None and "Salary" in df.columns:
                    metric = "Salary"

                if metric:

                    filtered_df = df[

                    # -------------------------------------

                    # -------------------------------------

                    if (
                        intent["aggregation"] == "mean"

                    ):

                        comparison = (
                            filtered_df

                        comparison = comparison.reindex(

                        difference = (

Metric:
{metric}

Dimension:

                    # -------------------------------------

                    comparison = comparison.reindex(

                    return f"""
Verified calculation:

Metric:
{metric}

Dimension:
{dimension}

Comparison:

Aggregation:

Difference:
{difference}
"""

    # =====================================================
    # 2. TOTAL
    # =====================================================

    if (
        "total" in question
        and (
            "sales" in question
            or "revenue" in question
            or "amount" in question
            or "value" in question
            or "salary" in question
        )
    ):

        metric = find_numeric_column(

        )

        if metric:

            total = df[metric].sum()

            return f"""

Metric:
{metric}

Total:
{total}
"""

    # =====================================================
    # 3. AVERAGE
    # =====================================================

    if (
        "average" in question
        or "mean" in question
        or "avg" in question
    ):

        metric = find_numeric_column(
            df,
            question
        )

        if metric:

            average = df[metric].mean()

            return f"""
Verified calculation:

Metric:
{metric}

Average:

    # =====================================================

    if (
        "highest" in question

        or "most" in question

        metric = find_numeric_column(

Highest Value:

    # =====================================================

    if (

# NORMALIZATION
# =========================================================

def _normalize(value):
    return re.sub(
        r"\s+",
        " ",
        str(value).strip().lower()
    )


def _clean_columns(df):
    df = df.copy()

    df.columns = [
        str(column).strip()
        for column in df.columns
    ]

    return df


# =========================================================
# COLUMN DETECTION
# =========================================================

def _find_column(df, candidates):
    """
    Find a dataset column using exact and partial matching.
    """

    normalized = {
        _normalize(column)
        .replace(" ", "")
        .replace("_", ""): column
        for column in df.columns
    }

    # Exact match
    for candidate in candidates:

        key = (
            _normalize(candidate)
            .replace(" ", "")
            .replace("_", "")
        )

        if key in normalized:
            return normalized[key]

    # Partial match
    for column in df.columns:

        column_key = (
            _normalize(column)
            .replace(" ", "")
            .replace("_", "")
        )

        for candidate in candidates:

            candidate_key = (
                _normalize(candidate)
                .replace(" ", "")
                .replace("_", "")
            )

            if (
                candidate_key
                and candidate_key in column_key
            ):
                return column

    return None


def _numeric_columns(df):
    return (
        df
        .select_dtypes(include="number")
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )


def _categorical_columns(df):
    return (
        df
        .select_dtypes(
            include=[
                "object",
                "category",
                "string"
            ]
        )
        .columns
        .tolist()
    )

    q = _normalize(question)

    patterns = [

        r"\bcomparison\b",
        r"\bversus\b",
        r"\bvs\b",
        r"\bdifference between\b",
        r"\bcompare between\b",
    ]

    return any(
        re.search(pattern, q)
        for pattern in patterns
    )


def _average_requested(question):

    q = _normalize(question)

    return any(
        word in q
        for word in [
            "average",
